title: Omitting the owner pronoun with several things
summary: Leave out meidän or teidän while keeping the noun ending; retain heidän with plural possessed nouns.
targetSkills: Possessive pronoun omission and clear reference
prerequisiteSkills: Plural possessed nouns in ownership sentences
objectives: Leave out meidän or teidän while keeping the noun ending; retain heidän with plural possessed nouns.
Apply the pattern using the supporting forms shown.

sections.title: Keep the ending when omitting the pronoun
paragraphs: Leave out meidän or teidän while keeping the noun ending; retain heidän with plural possessed nouns.
Nämä ovat teidän kirjanne. and Nämä ovat kirjanne. mean the same thing: “These are your books”. Plural -t drops before the possessive ending.
In these identification sentences retain heidän: its third-person ending does not identify the intended owner by itself. Omission in other sentence structures is outside this lesson.
Follow an explicit request to omit or retain the owner pronoun. Otherwise both ordinary first- and second-person forms are accepted.

steps: Nämä ovat (“These are”) identifies several things.
The ending identifies the owner, so omit meidän while retaining the noun ending.
Nämä ovat (“These are”) identifies several things.
The ending identifies the owner, so omit teidän while retaining the noun ending.
Nämä ovat (“These are”) identifies several things.
Retain heidän in this identification pattern so the owner stays clear.

commonMistakes: Omitting the owner pronoun does not remove its noun ending.
Retain heidän in this bounded identification pattern.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Write “These are our pillows.” in Finnish. Begin with Nämä ovat. Leave out meidän; keep the noun ending. Use tyyny (“pillow”).
practiceExercises.explanation: Nämä ovat identifies several things. The ending -mme identifies our ownership. Meidän can be omitted because the ending identifies the owner; the suffix stays.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: demonstrative + agreeing olla + optional owner pronoun + possessed noun

parts.formation: Nämä is the plural of tämä: several things.
Use ovat with several things, independently of how many people own them.
tyynyt (“pillows”) loses its plural -t before -mme: tyyny + -mme = tyynymme. The ending identifies the owner, so meidän can be left out.

answerDiagnostics.explanation: Drop the noun’s plural -t before -mme: use tyynymme.
Keep the possessive ending -mme even when the owner pronoun is present or omitted.
Meidän needs -mme; changing the ending changes the owner.
These are several things: Nämä needs ovat, regardless of the number of owners.

Heidän is the personal owner form of he; it selects -nsa.
kissat (“cats”) loses its plural -t before -nsa: kissa + -nsa = kissansa.
